title: He wasn’t the chosen one.
paragraphs: And that should disturb your theology… in the best way.

Because some of us were taught that if you’re not “Isaac,” you don’t get attention.
If you’re not the promise, you’re just the problem.
If your life started in mess, you’ll always be marked by it.

Not later.
Not after he “fixed himself.”
Not when his story looked clean enough to be preachable.
Genesis says, “God heard the voice of the boy” (Genesis 21:17).

The boy born from impatience…
The child tied to someone else’s compromise…
The one history would call “the other son”…
So what does that mean for you?
Because if we’re honest—some of us feel like Ishmael.

Not chosen.
Not first.
Not clean.

You show up to church, but there’s a quiet voice saying, “You’re not really part of this.”
You pray, but it feels like your words hit the ceiling.
You obey… halfway.
You delay… quietly.
You compromise… just enough to keep your image intact.
Here’s the tension we don’t like to admit:

Sometimes we’re not suffering because life is unfair…
We’re suffering because we’re living in the ripple of disobedience—ours or someone else’s.

Abram and Sarai rushed God.
They manufactured a solution.
And Ishmael was born into a decision he didn’t make.

You’re carrying emotional weight that didn’t start with you.
Family dysfunction.
Generational wounds.
Silent rejection.
God’s ability to hear you is not limited by the mess that formed you.
God hearing Ishmael didn’t mean God approved everything around him.
And this is where many people get it wrong.

You want God’s attention…
Without God’s authority.

You want Him to hear your cry…
But not confront your sin.
If you only want God to respond—but not to rule—you don’t want salvation. You want convenience.
Because Ishmael’s story shows us something powerful—but incomplete.
But hearing is not the finish line.
Because this is where grace walks in.

The same God who heard a crying boy in the desert…
Stepped into human history through Jesus Christ.
Because your deepest problem isn’t rejection.

Not just what was done to you—
But what lives inside you.

Scripture says, “All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God” (Romans 3:23).
Not some.

That includes the “good ones.”
The “religious ones.”
The ones who know how to look holy but hide pride, lust, bitterness, or quiet rebellion.
“While we were still sinners, Christ died for us” (Romans 5:8).

Not when you got your act together.
Not when you cleaned your image.
Jesus didn’t just hear your cry.

He took your sin.
Your shame.
Your hidden compromises.
Your delayed obedience.
Then He rose again—proving sin doesn’t get the final word.

Out of hiding.
Out of compromise.
Out of spiritual half-living.

Are you still living like Ishmael—defined by the wilderness?
Or are you ready to walk into what only Christ can give?

You are not just someone God hears.
In Christ, you become someone God adopts.

From outsider…
To son.
To daughter.

Not by birth.
Not by effort.
And here’s the revelation that will change everything:

Being heard by God is mercy.
Being saved by Jesus is everything.
If this is hitting you… it’s not random.

Not tomorrow.
Not “when things settle down.”

Talk to Him.
Confess what you’ve been hiding.
Lay down what you’ve been protecting.
Surrender what you’ve been delaying.
Because this journey doesn’t end with a post.
And next time, we’re going deeper into the moment God doesn’t just hear…
Check the comments. There’s something waiting for you there.
